items.title: Max Verstappen and George Russell rivalry "really cool for the sport", says F1 pundit
items.summary: The Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend reignited the long-running tension between Red Bull and Mercedes drivers, Max Verstappen and George Russell, and it was the talking point of Sky's F1 Show podcast this week.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton on latest Charles Leclerc flashpoint: "We're going to figure it out"
items.summary: Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton says he is confident he and team-mate Charles Leclerc will "figure it out" following their latest on-track skirmish at last week's Las Vegas GP.

items.title: Charles Leclerc refuses to reveal Ferrari's "rules of engagement" after Lewis Hamilton crash
items.summary: Charles Leclerc walked into Thursday’s FIA press conference at the Losail International Circuit knowing the spotlight would stay locked on Ferrari’s garage.

items.title: Charles Leclerc urges "solution" after several clashes with Lewis Hamilton
items.summary: Charles Leclerc was left furious by those ‘questioning his integrity and love for Ferrari’ after yet another clash with Formula 1 team-mate Lewis Hamilton - having urged to find a “solution”. The Ferrari pair have been at loggerheads several times during the second half of the 2026 F1 campaign, clashing at Monza, Zandvoort and Mexico before their latest spat in Las Vegas.

items.title: David Croft: Max Verstappen has Fernando Alonso's race intelligence but is faster
items.summary: Sky Sports Formula 1 lead commentator David Croft sees Fernando Alonso's smart racing in Max Verstappen, but adds that the four-time champion has more speed. Speaking on Sky Sports' F1 Show podcast after Verstappen's Las Vegas Grand Prix win, Croft was asked to sum up what he had seen from the Red Bull driver.

items.title: George Russell: Max Verstappen comments "amusing", but I stand by what I said
items.summary: Two years after their last major spat around this time of the year, Russell and Verstappen clashed again last week in Vegas after an impeding incident in free practice that infuriated the Briton, with Verstappen ruining the Mercedes driver's lap by passing him into the last corner - an unwritten rule that the Dutchman doesn't tend to mind breaking.

items.title: George Russell shrugs off Max Verstappen’s Las Vegas remarks: “Certain things really made me laugh”
items.summary: George Russell arrived at the Losail International Circuit on Thursday refusing to pour fresh fuel on Formula 1’s loudest driver feud - though he made it clear he was not retracting a word of what started it.

items.title: F1 2027 grid: Who will be racing and where? The full line-up
items.summary: The 2027 Formula 1 grid is now complete following the announcement from Haas that it has retained star youngster Oliver Bearman. But the American squad is also the only team that is altering its driver pairing for next season, as many potentially enthralling storylines failed to materialise. So, here’s a look at the situation.

items.title: Fernando Alonso to miss Qatar F1 media day with viral illness
items.summary: Fernando Alonso will be absent from Formula 1's media day ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix as he recovers from a "viral infection". The two-time champion will miss the traditional media obligations at the Lusail International Circuit as he aims to return to fitness for first practice on Friday.

items.title: Fernando Alonso: ‘I will quit F1 when I feel slow, not at a specific age’
items.summary: Fernando Alonso says he will quit Formula 1 when he feels slow and he doesn’t need to be as fit as a football player to be competitive. Alonso is the most experienced driver in F1’s history, having competed in 23 seasons from 2001 to 2026, and the two-time champion has maintained his involvement well beyond his peers’ retirement age despite his current 245-race winless streak.

items.title: McLaren flags the crucial early-stop trap inside Qatar’s raised 27-lap rule
items.summary: Formula 1 returns to the Losail International Circuit this weekend with a familiar strategic guardrail - and a subtly shifted trap waiting right after lights out.

items.title: Oliver Bearman locks in Haas F1 seat as 2027 grid officially set
items.summary: Oliver Bearman will officially stay at Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season after he and the team finally put pen to paper on a new deal. The American squad announced the renewal on Thursday, meaning the 21-year-old Briton will partner Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara at Haas next season.

items.title: Nico Rosberg rules George Russell out of 2027 F1 title fight: “Dug himself into a mental hole”
items.summary: George Russell entered the 2026 Formula 1 campaign looking every bit like Mercedes’ undisputed leader. Nine months later, former Silver Arrows world champion Nico Rosberg does not even consider the 28-year-old a championship contender for next season.

items.title: Max Verstappen admits he would “rather stay at home” ahead of Qatar and Abu Dhabi
items.summary: Formula 1’s paddock is touching down in Doha for the penultimate round of the 2026 championship, yet Max Verstappen is not pretending the trip sits easily with him. Speaking to Dutch outlet De Telegraaf, the four-time world champion delivered a blunt assessment of finishing the 23-race calendar in Qatar and Abu Dhabi amid ongoing regional hostilities. "Do I feel comfortable with it?

items.title: FIA filings reveal the Red Bull aero update behind Max Verstappen’s Las Vegas GP win
items.summary: Max Verstappen’s Las Vegas Grand Prix victory played out like a high-speed chess match on battery deployment, yet the race-winning foundation rested on a much quieter aerodynamic fix.

items.title: Fred Vasseur is running out of answers at Ferrari, says Jolyon Palmer
items.summary: In a 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix where 22 drivers traded a record 352 overtakes largely cleanly, Formula 1’s fiercest intra-team blowup still belonged to Ferrari.

items.title: Five things to look out for at F1’s Qatar GP
items.summary: The 2026 Formula 1 season is nearing its conclusion, with the Qatar Grand Prix taking place this weekend ahead of the Abu Dhabi finale next week. Both titles have already been decided with Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes clinching the drivers’ and constructors’ crowns. However, that doesn’t mean nothing is at stake, so here are five things to watch out for at Lusail.

items.title: Williams, Alpine fall foul of F1's 2025 cost cap
items.summary: The Williams and Alpine F1 teams have fallen foul of Formula 1's 2025 cost cap, reaching an Accepted Breach Agreement with the FIA, with Williams incurring a sporting penalty for overspending and Alpine handed a fine. The FIA announced on Wednesday that Williams overspent the 2025 cost cap by £627,000 or 0.48%.

items.title: Zak Brown rules out McLaren engine programme for F1 2030
items.summary: Zak Brown has ruled out a factory engine programme for the 2030 Formula 1 campaign as McLaren is “very happy” with its Mercedes partnership. The British marque has been a Mercedes customer since 2021 and has enjoyed vast success in that period, winning two constructors’ titles (2024, 2025), a drivers’ championship (2025) and 24 grands prix.

items.title: Fernando Alonso: “We can't be competitive with the power unit we have”
items.summary: Fernando Alonso says Honda is “a very long way behind” its Formula 1 rivals and Aston Martin therefore “can’t be competitive” with the Japanese engine, albeit expressing hope for the future. As F1 switched to power units featuring 47% electrical energy, Honda’s new powertrain has been lacking both power and reliability.

items.title: Lando Norris expects 2030 F1 racing to surpass Las Vegas GP spectacle
items.summary: Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix delivered a headline statistic built for highlight reels: 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes across 50 laps, shattering the championship’s all-time passing record. Yet runner-up Lando Norris was not fully sold on what that figure meant from inside the cockpit.

items.title: Unaired Las Vegas radio reveals Red Bull considered giving up Max Verstappen's lead
items.summary: In almost any other Formula 1 race, suggesting a race leader deliberately surrender first place with one lap left would sound unthinkable. At the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Red Bull’s pitwall genuinely floated the idea to Max Verstappen.

items.title: Jolyon Palmer: No rival could match Max Verstappen's fight against George Russell in Las Vegas
items.summary: Even in a Las Vegas Grand Prix packed with 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes, the defining moments of Max Verstappen’s victory came down to raw wheel-to-wheel nerve rather than battery spreadsheets.

items.title: Decision time looms for Colton Herta after 2027 Cadillac F1 snub
items.summary: Cadillac's decision to stick with veteran incumbent Valtteri Bottas to partner Sergio Perez is a choice for continuity and stability after a debut campaign plagued with issues for Formula 1's 11th team in 2026. It also raises key questions over what's next for Colton Herta.

items.title: The issue that cost Pierre Gasly a potential "win" at F1's Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Pierre Gasly reckons he potentially had the pace to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix, had a cooling issue not affected his Alpine Formula 1 car in the closing stages. The Frenchman finished fifth from eighth on the grid, but after 31 of the scheduled 50 laps, Gasly was third behind Red Bull’s eventual winner Max Verstappen and Mercedes’ George Russell.

items.title: F1 pundit calls for real consequences at Ferrari: "I'd chuck Ollie Bearman in for a race"
items.summary: After Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton collided for the second time in three races during the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the paddock debate quickly moved past who misjudged Turn 7 and onto a harder question: how can Ferrari actually stop it from happening again?

items.title: Juan Pablo Montoya explains how Red Bull outsmarted Mercedes at F1 Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Mercedes brought the fastest single-lap package to the Las Vegas Strip - newly crowned 2026 world champion Kimi Antonelli topped qualifying before a five-place engine penalty dropped him to sixth, while George Russell lined up alongside polesitter Max Verstappen.

items.title: Isack Hadjar frustrated – What really happened on Red Bull's team radio in Las Vegas
items.summary: Isack Hadjar started Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix from fourth on the grid, and by lap four he had already found himself running second, right behind Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen.

items.title: Max Verstappen jokes last time he won a race like F1 Las Vegas GP it was "Mario Kart"
items.summary: Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says the last time he won a race like the Las Vegas Grand Prix was when he was playing Mario Kart. The Red Bull driver converted pole position into his 75th grand prix win, and his third in Las Vegas, in a race that featured 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes.

items.title: Laurent Mekies: Keeping his emotions in check is giving Isack Hadjar “lap time”
items.summary: Isack Hadjar left the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix empty-handed after a Lap 26 front wing failure and a post-race 10-second safety car penalty relegated him to 15th, yet Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies saw something far more encouraging on the Strip.
